newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand ended an uneventful day slightly weaker on Friday and was poised for a fresh assault on key resistance levels early next week, dealers said.
At the finish, the currency was pegged at 4.5320/5370 against the dollar from 4.5315/5165 on Thursday.
The currency spent the morning session drifting slowly weaker to its day's worst level of 4.5370 bid on offshore and local importer dollar buying.

From around 0800 GMT, however, the currency was helped firmer by exporter dollar selling which carried it to a day's best of 4.5270 bid. Some traders said the Reserve Bank had stepped in at the weaker levels to help it firmer.
"We tested 4.54 where we saw some supply from our friends up north," one trader said in reference to the central bank which is based in Pretoria.
While dealers were still unable to offer a fundamental reason for the rand's three cent fall this week, they said the currency was expected to test the 4.55 level early next week.
"We always try the same level twice," one dealer said.
Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 7.0888/0988 against sterling from 7.0798/0921 overnight and at 0.3354/3360 marks from 0.3353/3358 marks previously.
Trade on the bond market was subdued as players continued to search for fresh direction.
"Its been a dull day with very narrow ranges," one trader said.
Initial expectations that August trade balance figures would provide a pointer were dashed when the South African Revenue Services announced it would release the data at 1200 GMT on Monday.
In the absence of the trade figures, players set their sights on money supply data due for release at 1500 GMT on Friday.
"If we get a poor M3 figure it could push the market higher," the trader said.
Economists predicted year-on-year M3 growth to increase to 15.7 percent from July's 14.69. Growth in private sector credit extension is seen slowing to 17.9 percent from 18.50 in July.
At the finish, the key R150 was pegged at 15.10 percent from 15.12 percent overnight.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 44.65 million rand worth of South African bonds on Thursday after selling 140.7 million rand on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 37.95 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date -- from 2.82 billion rand on Wednesday.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.70 to 15.90 percent, while 90-day BAs were unchanged at 15.15 to 15.30 percent.
The Reserve Bank quoted the daily shortage lower at 7.133 billion rand on Thursday from 6.989 billion rand on Wednesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
